headline: Primary Bathroom Remodeling Checklist: What to Prepare Before Construction
articleBody:
Planning an overhaul for your primary suite requires balancing personal comfort, long-term durability, and structural logistics. Walking through this checklist before purchasing finishes or signing agreements ensures your project runs smoothly.

- [ ] Precise room measurements — Confirm exact wall lengths, ceiling height, and door clearances before shopping for double vanities or freestanding tubs.
- [ ] Structural layout decision — Decide whether your existing toilet and shower drains will stay in place or move, which heavily dictates overall plumbing costs.
- [ ] Dedicated storage inventory — Catalog your linens, toiletries, and small appliances so custom cabinetry, medicine cabinets, and niches are sized accurately.
- [ ] Layered lighting plan — Map out task lighting at the vanity mirrors, ambient overhead recessed lights, and wet-rated shower lights on separate switches.
- [ ] Ventilation sizing verification — Check that the exhaust fan capacity matches the room's total cubic footage to prevent long-term condensation and mirror fogging.
- [ ] Waterproofing system selection — Specify an approved continuous waterproofing membrane behind custom tile showers, built-in benches, and shampoo niches.
- [ ] Building permit verification — Confirm with your contractor which electrical, plumbing, and layout alterations require Salt Lake Valley municipal permits and inspections.
- [ ] Material lead-time confirmation — Order tile, custom cabinetry, glass enclosures, and plumbing valves early to ensure everything arrives before demolition day.

How to use this checklist:
Review these points during your initial design phase. Settling mechanical layouts and storage requirements first prevents expensive mid-project revisions. When you are ready to remodel your primary bathroom, reach out to Blue Lake Construction at 385-202-5987 to get started.
